item.text: The search result points to the Diamond campground in Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest, facility `233869`. I’m going straight to Recreation.gov’s availability endpoint so I can read live date status instead of relying on the rendered page.
`jq` is not installed here, so I’m parsing the JSON with Python and scanning the per-site calendar for the first reservable nights.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json, urllib.request, collections
facility=233869
url=f'https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/availability/campground/{facility}/month?start_date=2026-05-01T00%3A00%3A00.000Z'
data=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(url))
counts=collections.Counter()
sites=collections.defaultdict(list)
for sid, site in data.get('campsites',{}).items():
    name=site.get('site') or sid
    for d, status in site.get('availabilities',{}).items():
        if status=='Available':
            day=d[:10]
            counts[day]+=1
            sites[day].append(name)
for day in sorted(counts)[:10]:
    print(day, counts[day], ', '.join(sorted(sites[day])[:10]))
PY"
